title: Christine Wonsley July 5, 2026 Facebook appeal — attached-media ledger

parentPost.author: Christine Wonsley
parentPost.visibleText: This is our Nolan Wells aka Nono. One of the sweetest and kindest souls you could ever meet. He went missing on Horn Island on July 4th. I’m looking for any pics or videos that was taken on the Northwest tip of Horn. Please help us find our sonshine.

scopeNote: This ledger preserves the 12 still-image attachments and one reel link surfaced in the loaded All comments view. A Facebook comment count can include replies and comments that the interface does not load or later removes; this is not represented as a forensic export of every comment. Visible Facebook times authenticate publication/display time only, not when an attached image was captured.

records.assessment: A contemporaneous public submission showing boats, a personal watercraft, and people in shallow water. The commenter labels it East Tip and July 4. No original file metadata, capture time, vessel identification, or Nolan identification is public. It concerns the east tip, not the northwest search/recovery area.

records.assessment: A repost preserving the same Matthew Lamp thread later shared by other commenters. It is not independent corroboration.

records.message: Mane that forshow look like a person
records.assessment: A screenshot of social-media users interpreting a distant pixel or wave as a possible person. It has no authenticated time, location, scale, original file, or reliable identification.
A screenshot of later media reporting about Katie and Nolan. It is not a contemporaneous witness statement and adds no independent source.
The parent comment contains only a reel link. The site does not auto-play external video, and no evidentiary claim is assigned without reviewing provenance and contents.

records.message: The photos from that night alone says alot.
records.assessment: A screenshot of Christine Wonsley’s separate post showing several July 4 group photographs. The comment’s interpretation is not evidence; the underlying photos remain useful media records whose exact capture times are not authenticated.

The screenshot attributes to Matthew Lamp that one passenger was pretty certain Nolan was part of a group that was almost fighting around 5 PM, that a blue-top Bertram left shortly afterward and fast, and that three people on Lamp’s boat said the dispute was among the group. This is Lamp relaying unnamed passengers, not Lamp claiming a personal sighting. The exact event time, vessel, participants, original thread, and passenger statements remain unverified.
A public news-style update stating that a body had been found and identity was not yet confirmed. Official and contemporaneous news records are stronger sources for the recovery chronology.

records.message: This what a man said happened on the boat !
records.assessment: A second screenshot of the Matthew Lamp source chain. It gives more of the visible thread and shows Christine Wonsley being tagged, but it does not independently corroborate the underlying passenger account.

records.message: racists, stop your demonic ranting. He was not with any of the guys when he disappeared. He was with a girl and then they parted ways, so it sounds like an accident.
records.assessment: The attachment is a July 4 group photo that may help identify people, vessels, or surrounding boats. The commenter’s narrative is not presented as firsthand and is not evidence that the death was accidental. Exact photo time and provenance remain unauthenticated.
A screenshot of one image from Christine Wonsley’s July 4 photo set. The commenter’s distrust statement supplies no factual basis and is excluded from the evidence analysis.
